name: Somapacitan
lead: Somapacitan (brand name Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone derivative that binds reversibly to albumin, given by subcutaneous injection [1][2]. The US label covers pediatric patients aged 2.5 years and older with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), short stature born small for gestational age, Noonan syndrome growth failure and idiopathic short stature, as well as adults with GHD [12].

Phase 3 trials examined it in adults (REAL 1) and children (REAL 4), with long-term follow-up of the phase 2 REAL 3 study reaching four years [1][2][6][9]. Reviews describe non-inferior height velocity and a similar safety profile compared with daily growth hormone for the long-acting class [7].
It is a prescription medicine. One looksmax.org thread asks whether it is worth using, with no substantive discussion found.

paras: The US label lists pediatric GHD, short stature born small for gestational age without catch-up growth by age 2, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature in patients aged 2.5 years and older, and GH replacement in adults with GHD [12].

According to the label, somapacitan binds a dimeric GH receptor, with some effects mediated by liver-produced IGF-1 and others direct [12]. A study examined optimal monitoring of weekly IGF-I levels during once-weekly therapy [10].

The US labels for long-acting growth hormones list warnings including increased mortality in acute critical illness, severe hypersensitivity, increased risk of neoplasms (notably second neoplasms in childhood cancer survivors), glucose intolerance and diabetes mellitus, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism [12]. Label pregnancy information notes no human data, that published short-acting rhGH data have not identified a risk, and that animal studies were not teratogenic [12].

In children, a phase 2 dose-escalation trial and the REAL 3 phase 2 trial compared weekly somapacitan with daily GH, with three- and four-year results published [4][5][6][9]. The phase 3 REAL 4 trial randomised 200 treatment-naive children across 20 countries [1]. In adults, the phase 3 REAL 1 trial was placebo-controlled with an open-label daily-GH arm, and a 26-week safety trial and a trial in previously treated adults were also published [2][3][8]. Long-term surveillance studies are registered [13][14].
On looksmax.org, a user asked whether somapacitan is good and where pediatric growth hormone products can be obtained [11].

timeline.event: First human dose trial in healthy subjects starts [15].
REAL 1 adult phase 3 and REAL 3 child phase 2 results published [2][4].

card.summary: A weekly albumin-binding growth hormone for diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions; no data for height otherwise.
card.note: Prescription drug; trials in diagnosed conditions only.

quick.overview:
Somapacitan (Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection. In the US it is labelled for growth hormone deficiency in children and adults and for several pediatric short-stature conditions.

Trials compared it with daily growth hormone in diagnosed patients. No study has tested it for height or appearance in people without a diagnosis.
quick.mechanism: It is a growth hormone derivative that binds albumin reversibly, extending its action, and binds the GH receptor with effects partly mediated by IGF-1.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
